synopsis: EMDAP is the US nuclear regulator’s 20-step safety-analysis modeling process, documented in NRC RG 1.203 dated December 2005; its four elements cover requirements, an assessment base, model development and adequacy judgment [f14640, f8088, f14643, f14644, f14645]. PIRT ranks physical phenomena by importance and understanding, directing test evidence toward highly ranked phenomena and reducing emphasis on low-ranked ones [f14643, f7836, f14646]. Its assessment base combines separate-effects and integral-effects experiments, while Step 19 uses scaling, similarity and applicability analysis to justify applying test-facility evidence to the full-size plant or beyond the test matrix [f14644, f8090, f7901, f8091]. The booklet rates EMDAP the best model for phenomena ranking, uncertainty and validation-matrix discipline for off-road automatic braking, but explicitly says it is not proven in that application [f8093, f8094]. Accordingly, the booklet retains integral full-system tests after submodel validation and treats an assessor-quality package as substantially broader than simulator results alone [f8197, f8026].
